newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova, Dnestr rebels break impasse at talks - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Moldova, Dnestr rebels break impasse at talks - Tass.

text.p: Moldova and its separatist Dnestr region have made a breakthrough at talks on improving their relations which were shattered by fighting five years ago, Itar-Tass news agency said on Friday.

Tass quoted visiting Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov as saying months of deadlock had been broken at talks on Thursday night on normalising ties following the bloody clashes in 1992 over Dnestr's independence demands.

"A breakthrough has now been made in relations between Moldova and Dnestr," said Primakov, who was present at the talks in the Moldovan capital Chisinau between President Petru Lucinschi and Dnestr separatist leader Igor Smirnov.

The breakthrough came over a memorandum on normalising ties, which are still strained after 1992 clashes between separatists and Moldovan security forces killed hundreds of people before Russian peacekeeping troops intervened.
Lucinschi had refused to sign the memorandum unless it was altered to reflect the territorial integrity of the former Soviet republic of 4.3 million people.
Details of the breakthrough were not immediately available but Primakov and Lucinschi were expected to give a news conference after meeting for talks later on Friday.

Primakov said an article had been added to the memorandum saying the sides would "build their relations within the framework of a common state and within the framework of (the former) Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic's borders as of January 1990".
He said the memorandum would be signed in Moscow by May 15.
The mainly Russian-speaking Dnestr region, which is Moldova's industrial heartland, declared independence in 1990, fearing Moldovans wanted to unite with Romania.
No other state has recognised Dnestr's independence and Russian peacekeepers remain there.
